caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 202 of 2009.
lawyer:
Mr. AF Hassan Ariff Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
None represented ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Dr. Tapan Kumar Dey -----Petitioner
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
A Wahhab Miah J: The accused is the petitioner in this leave petition. The petitioner has challenged the judgment and order dated 12-3-2009· passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.10454 of 2008 discharging the Rule. 

 4. An officer of the Commission investigated the case and submitted charge-sheet against the petitioner on 27-5-2008 under section 26(2)(Ka) of the Ain, 2004 and made prayer for issuance of warrant of arrest and attachment of his property. After submission of charge-sheet, the record of the case was sent to the Senior Metropolitan Special Judge, Chittagong who by order dated 29-5-2008 took cognizance in the case and issued warrant of arrest against the petitioner (the case number of the Senior Metropolitan Special Judge is not available from the record). The petitioner surrendered before the Senior Metropolitan Special Judge, Chittagong on 04-6-2008, but he did not grant bail to the petitioner and was sent to jail hajat. On 11-6-2008, the petitioner filed an application before the Senior Metropolitan Special Judge under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) for discharging him from the case. On that very date, the case was transferred to the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong for trial and disposal. 

 5. The Divisional Special Judge took cognizance in the case against the petitioner on 16-6- 2008 and the case was renumbered as Special Case No.18 of 2008. The learned Divisional Special Judge by his order dated 19-6-2008 rejected the application of the petitioner filed under section 241A of the Code and framed charge against him on 29-6-2008. At this stage of the proceedings, the petitioner filed an application before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code for quashing the proceedings of the special case and obtained the Rule, At the time of issuance of the Rule, further proceedings of the case were stayed. 

 7. Mr. AF Hassan Ariff, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner relying upon a letter issued by the Head Officer of the Commission addressed to the petitioner vide Memo No. দুদক/২৩৪-২০০(বিঃঅনুঃ-২)/৬৬৭১/১ dated 29-4-2001 under the signature of Mubara Khanam, Deputy Director and a follow up letter issued by the Shamnnita District Office of the Commission, Chittagong dated 14-5- 2008 giving reference to the said letter of the Head Office submitted that after the issuance of the letter dated 29-4-2001 by the Commission to the effect that it filed the allegation (নথিভুক্ত) against the petitioner as per the recommendation made in the report, there was no reason to proceed with the case for the alleged commission of offence by the petitioner under section 26(2)(Ka) of the Ain, 2004 and the impugned proceeding is nothing but an abuse of the process of the Court and, as such, the same was liable to be quashed, the High Court Division erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order discharging the Rule. 

 9. So far as the submission of Mr. Hassan Ariff that the Commission having given a letter to the petitioner that it filed the allegation brought against him in view of the report submitted in the matter, prima-facie, proved that the petitioner committed no offence. Therefore, the impugned' proceeding is nothing but an abuse of the process of the Court. We are of the view that the letter allegedly issued from the Head Office of the Commission if so facto cannot be accepted as a proof of innocence of the petitioner of the allegations made against him. The letter has to be proved as per the rules of evidence at the trial. Further, the letter of the Commission was allegedly issued on 29-4-2008, whereas charge-sheet in the case was submitted on 27-5-2008. We failed· to understand how the Commission could issue such letter after submission of charge-sheet. It also appears that as per the provisions of section 33 of the Ain, 2004 it is the Commission which shall have a permanent prosecution unit consisting of necessary number of prosecutors for prosecuting the cases investigated by it and triable by the Special Judge. So, the Commission was a necessary party to be impleaded in the application filed before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code. And admittedly, it is the Commission which lodged the FIR and the charge- sheet was submitted in the case by its officer after investigation, but the Commission was not made a party in the miscellaneous case before the High Court Division. Therefore, the Commission had no chance to say its version on the letter allegedly issued by it. We like to observe further that In the context, the authenticity of the letter dated 29-4-2008 allegedly issued by the Head Office of the Commission .under the signature of Mubara Khanam, Deputy Director and her authority to issue such letter also need to be proved and examined respectively. The contents of the follow up letter issued by the Shamannita District Office of the Commission, Chittagong dated 14-5-2008 are also not similar to those of the letter issued by Head Office on 29-4-2008. 

 10. We have gone through the FIR and the charge-sheet. On perusal of the same, it appears to us that a clear prima-facie case has been made but therein against the petitioner under the first part of section 26(2)(Ka) of the Ain, 2004 making him liable for prosecution. In this regard, we also endorse the view of the High Court Division that "However, the question whether the accused-petitioner was really served with notice in time to respond or whether he was prevented by sufficient reasons from submitting wealth statement within the specified time, are essentially defence pleas and controversial facts which are to be decided by the trial Court on the basis of evidence to be adduced by the parties and there is no scope in the present forum to decide those controversial matters."
